name: Geum
latin: Geum quellyon 'Mrs J. Bradshaw' (also sold as Geum chiloense)
grown_as: The garden geum 'Mrs Bradshaw' from seed: a hardy perennial with semi-double scarlet flowers. Not Geum coccineum, which is smaller with single orange-red flowers.
habit: A clump of leaves 20 to 30 cm high and about 40 cm across, with thin, wiry, branched, hairy flower stems rising to 40 to 60 cm, the flowers dancing above the leaves.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette at the base; a few small leaves on the flower stems
leaf.type: Compound, pinnate in a lyre shape: a very large rounded end leaflet with several pairs of much smaller, uneven leaflets down the stalk, small and tiny ones alternating
leaf.leaflets: The end leaflet rounded to kidney-shaped, 5 to 10 cm across, shallowly three- to five-lobed; side leaflets small, oval, unequal. Stem leaves small, stalkless, three-lobed.
leaf.outline: Long and narrow overall, 15 to 30 cm including the stalk, the end leaflet by far the biggest part
leaf.base: End leaflet heart-shaped to rounded at its base
leaf.margin: Rounded teeth (scalloped) all round every leaflet and lobe
leaf.veins: End leaflet with several main veins spreading from its base like a hand, pressed in
leaf.stalk: Hairy, with the small leaflets spaced along it

flower.form: An open bowl to saucer, semi-double
flower.petals: About 10 to 15 in two or three rows, free, rounded, slightly wavy
flower.centre: A green-yellow dome of carpels ringed by many yellow stamens
flower.behind: Five green pointed sepals with five tiny extra ones between them, showing behind the petals
flower.carried: A few in loose branched sprays at the tops of wiry stems, facing up or out, with round buds

fruit: A compact, round, bristly head of small hairy seeds, each with a short hooked tail (the old style), green ripening reddish brown, like a small burr. Seeds small, flat, brown, with the bristly hooked tail.
seedling: Two small round seed leaves on stalks, then rounded, scalloped first leaves on long stalks
winter: A low, semi-evergreen rosette of leaves, the large end leaflets often bronzed.

leaf: a large rounded lobed end leaflet with much smaller uneven leaflets down the stalk
bloom: semi-double scarlet bowl with two or three rows of rounded petals
a green-yellow centre ringed by yellow stamens
seed: small flat brown seeds each with a long hooked tail
seedling: first true leaves rounded and scalloped
young: a low rosette of lyre-shaped leaves with big rounded end leaflets
flower: thin wiry branched stems holding scarlet flowers well above the leaves
a rosette of leaves at the base
seedhead: compact round bristly reddish-brown burrs of hooked seeds on the wiry stems
dormant: a low rosette of leaves, some bronzed

look_alikes: Wood avens (Geum urbanum), a common weed, has small yellow flowers and three-lobed leaflets. Water avens (Geum rivale) has nodding pink-orange bells. Geum coccineum is smaller with single orange-red flowers. Potentillas have five-fingered leaves.
